clue.text: Artist's backpay

indicators.note: the artist is back, meaning turned around to face the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: an artist is someone who draws, a drawer

explanation.surface: A painter finally receives the back wages owed to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backpay' reads as one word, but it splits: the artist's word is back, and pay is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in return for work or service, so it serves as payment.

clue.text: Chorus of "don'ts"?

definitions.note: plural noun for the verb: every don't is an order to hold back

blocks.note: first meaning: the repeated lines of a song
second meaning: a verb for abstaining, which is what each don't demands

explanation.surface: A crowd all chanting prohibitions at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and question mark flag that the second meaning is loose: each don't tells you to abstain.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated lines of a song are its chorus; the same word as a verb means abstain, the message of every don't.

clue.text: Not the best way to beat an opponent

blocks.note: first meaning: the opposite extreme, the poorest
second meaning: an old verb meaning to defeat

explanation.surface: A tactic for defeating a rival that is far from ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it is the superlative of bad; as a verb it means to get the better of someone.

clue.text: Dry off and smooth with sandpaper

blocks.note: first meaning: towel oneself vigorously after bathing
second meaning: sand a surface flat before painting

explanation.surface: Instructions for finishing woodwork after it gets wet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both towelling a body vigorously and abrading a surface flat before painting.

clue.text: One member to take part in strike

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament
to take a part in a play is to act

explanation.surface: A single union member is urged to join a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but here it means a blow or collision.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the forceful collision of one object hitting another, a blow.

clue.text: Compensate with cosmetics?

blocks.note: first meaning
second meaning: face paint and powder

explanation.surface: Covering a flaw with a dab of foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to make amends; as a noun it names lipstick, powder and foundation.

clue.text: Gypsum and basalt are different

indicators.note: being different means changed from how they stand, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A geologist notes that two rocks are not alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The white translucent stone used for carving is a fine-grained variety of the mineral calcium sulphate.

clue.text: She turns eastern hearts

indicators.note: turning the letters around shakes them into a new order

blocks.note: abbreviation for east
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman wins over people from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so any female person named that could be referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: State it is lent, hence restitution is required

indicators.note: restitution means restoring something, so the letters must be put back into a proper order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange, the comma ignored

explanation.surface: A country has lent money and now demands repayment.
explanation.definitionFit: The small Alpine principality between Switzerland and Austria is a sovereign country.

clue.text: A long way off getting a return of service

indicators.note: a return sends something back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone far away waits for a tennis serve to be sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' sounds like tennis, but it is one of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at or to a great distance, matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Workman who naturally works his way up

definitions.text: Workman who naturally works his way up

blocks.clueFragment: Workman who naturally works his way up
blocks.note: surface reading: an ambitious employee climbing the career ladder
setter's reading: a builder literally rises course by course as the wall he builds grows

explanation.surface: An ambitious labourer rises through the ranks on talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works his way up' sounds like promotion, but this builder climbs as each course of a wall goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who builds walls from fired clay blocks and mortar must rise as each row goes on.

clue.text: Military show leaves a permanent impression on one

definitions.text: leaves a permanent impression on one
definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: an evening display by soldiers and bands, like the Edinburgh one

blocks.clueFragment: leaves a permanent impression on one
blocks.note: second meaning: ink pricked into the skin that never fades

explanation.surface: A regimental display so stirring that spectators never forget it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an outdoor army pageant with bands and an indelible inked design on someone's skin.

clue.text: Struggles to maintain faith in the past

definitions.text: to maintain faith in the past
definitions.note: a description of the historical wars rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: vigorous campaigns for a cause

blocks.clueFragment: to maintain faith in the past
blocks.note: second meaning: the medieval Christian military expeditions to the Holy Land

explanation.surface: Keeping one's beliefs alive in bygone times was a constant battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigns for a cause are named after the medieval holy wars fought by Christian knights over Jerusalem.

clue.text: Cause to appear in bodily form when in a trance, perhaps

definitions.text: Cause to appear in bodily form

indicators.note: perhaps marks the words as only one possible arrangement, inviting another ordering

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A medium in a trance makes a spirit materialise in the flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to incarnate is to embody, giving a spirit or idea a physical human shape.

clue.text: Ballet posture of Lincoln in square dance

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new arrangement
in places one name inside the other letters

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
Abraham Lincoln was known as Abe

explanation.surface: A US president strikes a ballet pose at a hoedown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square dance' reads as one folk dance; the second word is the instruction to shuffle the first.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet this is a pose on one leg with the other extended straight behind.

clue.text: Stake for backing hotly-tipped runner

definitions.note: a cryptic description: a volcano with a hot summit down which lava runs

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: A punter places a bet on the racehorse everyone is tipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotly-tipped runner' looks like a racing favourite; it is a Sicilian volcano whose peak is hot and whose lava runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna in Sicily is an active volcano: its summit is literally hot and molten rock flows down its slopes.

clue.text: Trial run in the theatre

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following word

blocks.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: A dress rehearsal staged at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters sit in the middle of t-HEAT-re.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat is a preliminary race or round that decides who goes through to the final.

clue.text: Pope with aspiration to become emperor

blocks.note: an aspirate is an h sound, breathed out
Adrian IV was the only English pope

explanation.surface: An ambitious pontiff hopes to rise to imperial rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' looks like ambition, but it is a breathed h.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler who built the famous wall across northern Britain held the imperial title.

clue.text: Pipes may be severely tested

definitions.note: a cryptic description of where tobacco pipes are kept

blocks.note: first meaning: tobacco pipes are stored standing in a stand on a shelf
second meaning: suffering great strain, as on the medieval torture frame

explanation.surface: Plumbing is subjected to harsh pressure checks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means under great stress, from the torture device that stretched victims, and also where a smoker's pipes rest.

clue.text: Can holy orders be so calm and peaceful?

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asks whether religious brotherhoods can be truly serene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy orders' suggests monks; 'orders' is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are tranquil ones, from the mythical kingfisher said to still the sea while nesting.

clue.text: It makes light work of passing course

definitions.note: a cryptic description of electricity powering a lamp
a description, a flow moving along

blocks.note: first meaning: electricity flowing makes a bulb shine
second meaning: a flow of water or air moving along its path

explanation.surface: Something that breezes through a passing training module.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light work' reads as easy work, but it means making a lamp work.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity flowing through a wire powers lamps, and the same word names a stream's moving flow.

clue.text: Group of soldiers in particular

blocks.note: first meaning: a small squad assigned to a special duty
second meaning: an individual item or point

explanation.surface: A specific unit of troops is singled out.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a squad sent on a special task and a single small fact or point.

clue.text: Disciple has to stick by holy writ

blocks.note: to adhere is to stick
the New Testament

explanation.surface: A follower must keep faithfully to scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or supporter of a teacher, cause or faith, which is exactly what this noun names.

clue.text: Left one extremely out of sorts

blocks.note: abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one
both mean to a high degree

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned and alone feels thoroughly miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: Livery here is the adjective, an old word for liverish: irritable, as if one's liver were upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish or livery describes feeling unwell and bad-tempered, once blamed on a disordered liver.

clue.text: Speak evil about none

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: vice is wickedness
zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody may say a word about wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it in words, to utter or say it.

clue.text: Exclude underworld leader with pass

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
to pass a test is to qualify

explanation.surface: A gang boss is barred despite holding an entry permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld leader' suggests a crime boss, but it is the classical ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disqualify someone is to bar them from a competition or office, ruling them out.

clue.text: Piece of news I encountered on return

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to encounter someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A traveller picks up some gossip after coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is a single report or story in a bulletin or paper.

clue.text: An old record-player

blocks.note: surface reading: a vintage gramophone
setter's reading: the small part that actually plays the record by running in its groove

explanation.surface: A vintage gramophone from the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole machine is suggested, but only the steel point that runs in the groove is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: On old gramophones a sharp steel point tracked the groove and reproduced the sound, so it truly played records.

clue.text: Firm plan

blocks.note: first meaning: resolved, determined
second meaning: an aim or purpose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for being resolutely set on something and a noun for one's purpose or aim.
